1.2.3.7-f1.accuracy_reason: The source is Horace, Epistles 1.2.58–59, which begins with 'invidia'. Burton's sidenote reads only 'Hor.'

1.2.3.7-f13.accuracy_reason: The Vulgate Psalm 72:3 reads 'quia zelavi super iniquos', so Burton's Latin is not the Vulgate wording.

1.2.3.7-f4.accuracy_reason: The lines are Ovid, Metamorphoses 2.775–776, his portrait of Invidia.

1.2.3.7-f6.accuracy_reason: Ovid, Metamorphoses 2.780–2, reads 'intabescitque videndo / successus hominum carpitque et carpitur una / suppliciumque suum est'. So Burton's dash does leave out 'carpitque et carpitur una'.
